title: Small Bathroom Renovation: 5 Upgrades That Matter Most
audience: First-time homeowners anywhere in the world who are renovating a small bathroom on a tight budget.
brief: Walk through five budget-friendly upgrades in priority order, with practical steps for each. Friendly, encouraging tone for nervous first-timers. Goal: viewers download the free renovation checklist at reno.example/checklist.

issues.description: The opening spends about twenty seconds on greetings and throat-clearing without saying what the video covers; the actual topic only arrives afterwards.
The intro promises an exact itemised budget breakdown at the end, but the closing section gives only vague generalities and no numbers. The promise is never paid off.
Dense trade jargon (efflorescence, decoupling membrane, thermostatic mixing valve) is used with no explanation for a first-timer audience.

Claims a standard interior bathroom door is thirty-six inches wide. In fact common interior doors are twenty-eight to thirty-two inches; thirty-six inches is typical for exterior doors. Correct clearances should use twenty-eight to thirty-two inches.
Claims a forty-dollar tin of anti-mould paint guarantees no mould ever, whatever the ventilation. No paint can guarantee that; ventilation and moisture control matter more than any coating.
Re-explains how to use a tape measure three times in slightly different words, stalling the video for over half a minute.
A roughly forty-second story about a neighbour's farmhouse sink has no connection to small-bathroom upgrades on a budget and stalls the tutorial.
The brief's goal is downloads of the free renovation checklist, but the video ends with a plain sign-off and never mentions the checklist.
